comment: Brian VO Ep32 (300s): USA vs Australia, real kickoff Fri 19 Jun 2026 22:00. VERIFIED: USA — at the 1950 World Cup, a team of part-time amateurs beat mighty England 1-0 in Belo Horizonte (the 'Miracle on Grass'), Haitian-born Joe Gaetjens scoring the 37th-minute winner off a Walter Bahr cross — still one of sport's greatest upsets; USA reached the 2002 quarter-finals; co-hosts of 2026 under Mauricio Pochettino. AUSTRALIA (Socceroos) — on 16 Nov 2005 beat Uruguay on penalties (after 32 years away), John Aloisi the iconic winning spot-kick, keeper Mark Schwarzer saving two; left Oceania to join the AFC in 2006; reached the 2022 Round of 16. Stars USA: Christian Pulisic, Folarin Balogun, Giovanni Reyna, Tyler Adams, Weston McKennie. Australia: Mathew Ryan (GK/capt), Harry Souttar, Jackson Irvine, Cristian Volpato, Nestory Irankunda. lines.text: In nineteen fifty, a team of part-time amateurs walked out to face mighty England. Nobody gave them a prayer.
Ninety minutes later they had won one-nil — and a newspaper desk assumed the score was a typo. They called it the Miracle on Grass. And tonight, its ghost is watching.
Last time, we predicted Mexico would edge South Korea two-one. Tonight: the home of the greatest upset ever... against the bravest qualifiers in football.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends, episode thirty-two. The United States versus Australia. The co-hosts... against the Socceroos.
And stay with me — because both of these nations own a World Cup night that belongs in legend.
First, the history. And it is true. Belo Horizonte, Brazil, nineteen fifty. The United States against England, the kings of the game.
The thirty-seventh minute. A cross from Walter Bahr, and Joe Gaetjens — born in Haiti — flings himself at it.
One-nil. The amateurs had beaten the masters. It remains one of the greatest upsets in the history of sport.
Decades later they reached a World Cup quarterfinal, and now, as co-hosts, a golden generation carries the dream again.
Christian Pulisic, Weston McKennie, Tyler Adams — Americans starring at the biggest clubs in Europe.
And across from them — Australia. The Socceroos. A team that has done it the hard way, every single time.
Two thousand five. Thirty-two years without a World Cup. One night, against Uruguay, to end the wait.
It went to penalties. Schwarzer saved. And John Aloisi buried the kick that sent a nation into delirium.
The first team ever to reach a World Cup through a shootout. Then they left Oceania, and made the world take them seriously.
In twenty twenty-two they reached the knockouts again — proof the Socceroos never, ever stop fighting.
Now, the USA. Christian Pulisic — captain, talisman, the heartbeat of this team.
Folarin Balogun leads the line. Giovanni Reyna brings the magic. Tyler Adams and Weston McKennie drive the engine.
A generation built to make a home World Cup unforgettable.
But Australia have grit and giants. Captain Mathew Ryan, a goalkeeper at his fourth World Cup.
Harry Souttar towers at the back. Jackson Irvine never stops. And young Nestory Irankunda brings the spark.
So here is the duel. American flair and home advantage... against the unbreakable spirit of the Socceroos.
Our prediction — built on American talent, on a home crowd roaring them on, and on an Australia side that simply will not break. Watch.
The USA start strong. Reyna threads it through, and Christian Pulisic finishes with ease. One-nil.
But you do not take your eyes off Souttar at a set-piece. He climbs, and heads Australia level. One-all.
Then American quality tells. A cross, and Folarin Balogun powers home the winner. Two-one.
Two-one at the whistle, in our story. The USA edge it — but the Socceroos make them earn every inch.
Do you agree? Comment USA if the hosts have too much. Comment SOCCEROOS if Australia's spirit shocks them.
And that ghost in the stands? Legend number thirty-two: the Ghost of Belo Horizonte. He saw amateurs humble the masters.
Seventy-six years he has waited for another miracle. Tonight he came to see if lightning strikes twice. Collect him inside the game.
Which brings us to YOU. At WorldCup twenty-six dot world, pick three of the forty-eight nations — and every goal they score scores for you.
Free to play. Climb the leaderboard, just for fun. No prizes. Hit like, send this to a friend, and subscribe — the legends are only beginning.
